text: Miten kuukausittaiset maksut kehittyivät, ja mikä kuukausi oli paras kokonainen kuukausi?

result.reply:
**Lyhyesti:** Paras kokonainen kuukausi oli **maaliskuu 2018**, jolloin maksuja kertyi **622 AUD** (35 tilausta). Tammikuusta helmikuuhun maksut laskivat ja maaliskuussa nousivat selvästi.

| Kuukausi (2018) | Maksut (AUD) | Tilauksia | Keskimääräinen tilaus (AUD) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tammikuu | 496 | 29 | 17,10 |
| Helmikuu | 415 | 27 | 15,37 |
| Maaliskuu | 622 | 35 | 17,77 |
| Huhtikuu (vain 2.–9.4.) | 139 | 8 | 17,38 |

- **Kehitys:** Helmikuu oli noin 16 % tammikuuta heikompi. Maaliskuu oli noin 50 % helmikuuta vahvempi, ja sekä tilausmäärä että keskiostos kasvoivat.
- **Huhtikuu** on osittainen, koska aineisto päättyy 9.4.2018, joten sitä ei voi verrata kokonaisiin kuukausiin.

**Huomioitavaa:**
- Aineisto on historiallinen ja synteettinen esimerkkidata, ja se kattaa vain vuoden 2018 alkupuolen. Uudempaa dataa ei ole saatavilla, joten lukuja ei voi tulkita nykyisen liiketoiminnan kuvana. Haluatko, että jatkan tällä ajanjaksolla?
- Luvut ovat maksettuja summia, eivätkä ne ole nettotuloa. Ne sisältävät myös kupongit ja lahjakortit, ja palautetut tilaukset ovat mukana. Jos haluat nettotuloa tai vain valmistuneet tilaukset, kerro se, niin rajaan luvut sen mukaan.

models.name: customers
models.description: This table has basic information about a customer, as well as some derived facts based on a customer's orders
models.grain: One row per customer, including customers with no orders.

models.name: orders
models.description: This table has basic information about orders, as well as some derived facts based on payments

output.name: orders
output.description: This table has basic information about orders, as well as some derived facts based on payments
output.sql:
with order_payments as (
    select
        order_id,
        sum(case when payment_method = 'credit_card' then amount else 0 end) as credit_card_amount,
        sum(case when payment_method = 'coupon' then amount else 0 end) as coupon_amount,
        sum(case when payment_method = 'bank_transfer' then amount else 0 end) as bank_transfer_amount,
        sum(case when payment_method = 'gift_card' then amount else 0 end) as gift_card_amount,
        sum(amount) as amount
    from "jaffle_shop"."main"."stg_payments"
    group by order_id
)

select
    orders.order_id,
    orders.customer_id,
    orders.order_date,
    orders.status,
    order_payments.credit_card_amount,
    order_payments.coupon_amount,
    order_payments.bank_transfer_amount,
    order_payments.gift_card_amount,
    order_payments.amount
from "jaffle_shop"."main"."stg_orders" as orders
left join order_payments
    on orders.order_id = order_payments.order_id

joins: orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id (many orders to one customer).

metrics.amount: Sum of all recorded payments for this order in AUD, including coupons and gift cards, regardless of order status. Not net revenue or profit.
metrics.order_count: COUNT(*) on orders. For completed orders filter status = 'completed'.
metrics.average_order_amount: AVG(amount) on orders; excludes NULL amounts.

caveats: No refund ledger, tax breakdown, costs, or payment timestamps are available.
order_date is the order placement date, not the payment date.
The bundled seeds are historical synthetic data. Inspect MIN/MAX(order_date) before choosing dates.

columns.name: order_id
columns.description: This is a unique identifier for an order

columns.name: customer_id
columns.description: Foreign key to the customers table

columns.name: order_date
columns.description: Date (UTC) that the order was placed

columns.name: status
columns.description:
Orders can be one of the following statuses:

| status         | description                                                                                                            |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| placed         | The order has been placed but has not yet left the warehouse                                                           |
| shipped        | The order has ben shipped to the customer and is currently in transit                                                  |
| completed      | The order has been received by the customer                                                                            |
| return_pending | The customer has indicated that they would like to return the order, but it has not yet been received at the warehouse |
| returned       | The order has been returned by the customer and received at the warehouse                                              |

columns.name: credit_card_amount
columns.description: Amount of the order (AUD) paid for by credit card

columns.name: coupon_amount
columns.description: Amount of the order (AUD) paid for by coupon

columns.name: bank_transfer_amount
columns.description: Amount of the order (AUD) paid for by bank transfer

columns.name: gift_card_amount
columns.description: Amount of the order (AUD) paid for by gift card

output.name: customers
output.description: This table has basic information about a customer, as well as some derived facts based on a customer's orders
output.sql:
with customer_orders as (
    select
        customer_id,
        min(order_date) as first_order,
        max(order_date) as most_recent_order,
        count(*) as number_of_orders,
        sum(amount) as customer_lifetime_value
    from "jaffle_shop"."main"."orders"
    group by customer_id
)

select
    customers.customer_id,
    customers.first_name,
    customers.last_name,
    customer_orders.first_order,
    customer_orders.most_recent_order,
    customer_orders.number_of_orders,
    customer_orders.customer_lifetime_value
from "jaffle_shop"."main"."stg_customers" as customers
left join customer_orders
    on customers.customer_id = customer_orders.customer_id

meta.grain: One row per customer, including customers with no orders.
joins: customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id (one customer to many orders); aggregate order values before joining customer totals.

metrics.customer_lifetime_value: Lifetime payment amount in AUD across all orders, including returned orders; not net revenue. Use orders.amount for date-filtered totals.
metrics.number_of_orders: All orders placed by the customer, regardless of status.

columns.name: customer_id
columns.description: This is a unique identifier for a customer

columns.name: first_order
columns.description: Date (UTC) of a customer's first order

columns.name: most_recent_order
columns.description: Date (UTC) of a customer's most recent order

columns.name: number_of_orders
columns.description: Count of the number of orders a customer has placed

columns.name: customer_lifetime_value
columns.description: Lifetime recorded payments in AUD across all of the customer's orders, including returned orders. Not net revenue.

input.sql: select min(order_date) as min_date, max(order_date) as max_date, count(*) as orders from main.orders

output.sql: select min(order_date) as min_date, max(order_date) as max_date, count(*) as orders from main.orders

input.sql: select strftime(order_date, '%Y-%m') as month, count(*) as orders, round(sum(amount), 2) as payments_aud, round(avg(amount), 2) as avg_order_aud, min(order_date) as first_day, max(order_date) as last_day from main.orders group by 1 order by 1

output.sql: select strftime(order_date, '%Y-%m') as month, count(*) as orders, round(sum(amount), 2) as payments_aud, round(avg(amount), 2) as avg_order_aud, min(order_date) as first_day, max(order_date) as last_day from main.orders group by 1 order by 1
